title: Unsent Letter
description: This piece belongs to the Crimson and Scarlet series, an exploration of contemporary love discourse, unspoken emotions, and the fragile physical anchors of our deepest feelings. At the center of the composition is a visual motif of a crumpled letter painted in deep crimson and stark white. A sentence begins with the phrase “how many missed...” before dissolving into illegible marks and abstract texture. The letter serves as a universal symbol - a desperate attempt to bridge the distance between ourselves and the person we love, a tangible embodiment of the statement: “This is me, entirely.” When feelings become too overwhelming to process, the paper becomes an absorbent entity, soaking up every unspoken word, every doubt, and every surge of affection. By rendering this crumpled paper as an exhibit, the painting pauses a fleeting moment of intimacy and invites the viewer to step into the narrative, completing the fragment with their own history of unsent letters.
